source.title: On the Stability and Generalization of First-order Bilevel Minimax Optimization

record.tranche_reason: The study reports generalization-gap results for bilevel minimax optimization on a GAN image task, a setting outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures validation-to-test generalization gaps and how they change with iteration counts, meta-set size, and step-size schedules. It does not test memorization of random labels, ordinary natural-label classification, or the claim versions' architectures and measures.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes stability bounds and validation-to-test gaps in bilevel minimax GAN training. None of its results tests V1–V8. It cites Hoffer et al. and Keskar et al. when defining generalization gaps, but does not vary batch size or test their findings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive stability-based generalization bounds for SSGDA, TSGDA-1, and TSGDA-2, plus optimization-error and excess-risk bounds for SSGDA under convexity. Their single GAN task qualitatively supports dependence on meta-set size, iteration counts, and step-size schedules; these conclusions do not test V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes first-order bilevel minimax solvers and evaluates a bilevel GAN image task, rather than testing the listed memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or example-removal methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization outcome changes with iteration counts, meta-set size, and step-size schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: On Charlie Chaplin frame interpolation, excessive iteration counts can increase test error and the validation-to-test gap while reducing validation error. Larger meta sets and step-size choices affect generalization and convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization in bilevel minimax GAN training depends on meta-set size, inner and outer iteration counts, and step-size schedules.

record.problems: The empirical validation uses one image task and one solver; the text describes plotted results qualitatively without numerical values or reported error bars.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and their coexistence under the same training recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Effects of dropout, training-set size, augmentation, and removing dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures. Sample-replacement stability is a different construct.
Removing examples selected by label memorization and comparing retraining accuracy with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions; this does not dispute the unrelated qualitative findings. No verdict labels apply.

versions.untested_parts: Network width and test error past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.

rows.subject: specific GANs (Yao et al., 2024) with a bilevel reweighted strategy (Shu et al., 2019)
rows.operation_detail: Varied outer and inner iteration counts K and T using TSGDA-1.
rows.measure: Validation error, testing error, and generalization gap
rows.value: Excessive outer or inner iterations increased testing error and generalization gap while decreasing validation error.
rows.uncertainty: Average results after 10 independent repeats; no error bars or confidence intervals stated.
rows.note: The text describes the direction of change; plot values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The qualitative result is supported by Section 4.3(a), but measures none of V1–V8. Correct the iteration names: T denotes outer iterations and K inner iterations, as specified in Theorem 5 and the figure axes; Section 4.3(a) reverses them.

rows.subject: specific GANs (Yao et al., 2024) with a bilevel reweighted strategy (Shu et al., 2019)
rows.operation_detail: Varied meta-set size m1 and lower iteration count K, with T fixed.
rows.measure: Validation error, testing error, and generalization gap
rows.value: Slightly larger meta-set sizes could accelerate convergence and enhance generalization.
rows.uncertainty: Average results after 10 independent repeats; no error bars or confidence intervals stated.
rows.note: The authors qualify the improvement as applying to slightly larger meta-set sizes; plot values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The reported benefit of increasing meta-set size is supported, but measures none of V1–V8. Its qualified wording does not establish a partial effect for any listed version.

rows.subject: specific GANs (Yao et al., 2024) with a bilevel reweighted strategy (Shu et al., 2019)
rows.operation_detail: Compared fixed, decaying, and faster-decaying step-size schedules.
rows.value: Step-size selection critically affects generalization; faster-decayed step sizes reach convergence faster and more stably.
rows.uncertainty: Average results after 10 independent repeats; no error bars or confidence intervals stated.
rows.note: The paper gives this qualitative description; the figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The schedule comparison and qualitative convergence statement are supported, but do not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or measure any other listed version. Faster, more stable convergence alone does not establish lower held-out error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
